title: Compare useful reactive termini at equal macromer mass
statement: Under the declared model of one usable terminal acceptor per chain of molecular mass M>0, equal total macromer mass supplies candidate ends proportional to1/M. With useful association a, accessible-end fraction e, old-side targeting theta and individual service survival S, useful ends per mass are proportional to a*e*theta*S/M when other reaction/retention factors are held fixed.

requires: One usable terminus per actual macromer and a common molecular-mass convention; useful-end fractions and service survival must be justified.
Hold other catalytic/retention opportunities and the required mechanical function comparable, or account for their differences explicitly.
provides: Under the declared model of one usable terminal acceptor per chain of molecular mass M>0, equal total macromer mass supplies candidate ends proportional to1/M. With useful association a, accessible-end fraction e, old-side targeting theta and individual service survival S, useful ends per mass are proportional to a*e*theta*S/M when other reaction/retention factors are held fixed.
assumptions: The single-end premise is declared, not newly verified primary biochemistry. Branched/multiterminal designs change it.
Equal reactive-site counts are not equal supplied mass, manufacture, energy or sustained mechanical benefit.
costs: Charge actual macromer mass, terminal accessibility, association, correct-side reaction and later survival; long-chain retention can trade against fewer accessible ends.
contract.units: M is molecular mass in one fixed unit; a,e,theta,S are dimensionless; the opportunity density is inverse mass up to a common counting conversion.
contract.obstruction: Measure actual useful-end and load-survival factors at comparable mass before claiming the larger macromer is superior.

body: Count chains as supplied mass divided by molecular mass, then multiply by the declared useful-end factors. For long and short chains at otherwise equal factors, the long/short opportunity ratio is(M_short/M_long)*(a_long*e_long*theta_long*S_long)/(a_short*e_short*theta_short*S_short). The source's200-versus880 kDa example therefore needs more than4.4-fold improvement in the useful factor product to beat the shorter chain at equal mass. This is conditional counting, not measured association or an established polymer-length optimum. Multiple usable ends, changed accessibility/rates or different retained mechanical function require a different comparison. AFM adhesion-energy enhancement is not a shear-strength multiplier or a measurement of S.

evidence.range_scope: Declared single-terminus-per-chain mass-normalized accounting; conditional stoichiometric model.

review.scope: Completed source-exposed author reconstruction of uniform-window Poisson integration at k=d, the incomplete-gamma fixed-m expression and m/X tail, the one-hit small-time rate change, shared-anchor/contact ceiling under explicit independence, and conditional single-end mass accounting. New scientific response and the available original code were fully read statically, not executed. Earlier accepted two-hit units remain unchanged. The missing hybrid helper prevents acceptance of the reported optimum/Monte Carlo; cited primary studies, AFM-to-strength transfer, actual kinetics and physical welding/regeneration are not newly validated.
